Animal Vaccines

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Can South Africa's former world class immunology centre produce enough vaccines in time to prevent a countrywide epidemic or has the institution imploded on itself?

Unique Selling Point:
Why is a world class South African immunology centre not delivering much needed vaccines while scientists predict a country-wide epidemic?

Summary:
The wellbeing of the South African livestock sector is hanging in the balance amidst the heavy rain season that may result in a countrywide epidemic that can only be prevented by vaccination. But, are the enough vaccines available and why is the state mum?
The world class Onderstepoot Biological products vaccination plant was supposed to be upgraded in 2014 to enable it to research, produce and distribute much needed animal vaccinations. The highly specialised state owned veterinary science centre was given 500 million Rand to meet this need. It is the sole producer of vaccines that the agricultural sector cannot function without. And although the private sector produces the same vaccines, the state does not allow its distribution. Now it seems that no knows what happened to the money and whether the vaccine plant was upgraded at all.

Further information:
Imagine there was only one institution in the world able to produce vaccines that prevent devastating epidemics in animals and people? Well, Onderstepoort was that institution; the pride and joy of South Africa’s veterinary science. Now, there is not much left of this world class research centre and the worst is, the vaccines will be desperately needed this year. In 2022, cadre deployment, misappropriation of state funds reminiscent of the state capture years under Jacob Zuma will become painfully visible in the Agricultural sector. Scientists, organised agriculture, the SA red meat association, retailers and farmers are holding their breaths as the anticipation of the outbreak of Rift valley fever is lurking on the horizon. Given the heavy rainy season, scientists and experts predict that the virus can hit South Africa hard. Mosquito larvas that have been dormant in dams and lakes across the country for over 10 years during the extended drought, can hatch as soon as February and spread countrywide in a matter of weeks.
Rift Valley fever along with bluetongue disease and African horse sickness will cause mass devastation in the livestock sector if immediate solutions are not actioned and this will require decisive political will. Scientists and experts predict a massive shortage of vaccines for South Africa and the African continent at large. And that is all because of mismanagement of one of the country’s key scientific institutions. Treasury gave Onderstepoort Biological Products 500 million Rand in 2014 to develop a vaccine plant. This was never done. Instead 100 million was spent on the upgrading of offices and the payment of inflated salaries to people with no knowledge of vaccines or agriculture.
This cannot be fixed overnight. Luckily, top former scientists who departed from Onderstepoort developed a world class laboratory in Pretoria where the vaccines are being developed. Designedbiologix is able to avail vaccines for Rift Valley fever, bluetongue disease and horse sickness in time before the breakout, but government is not coming to the party. The laboratory has been waiting four years for its license. And now, it may be too late, except if the department of agriculture fast tracks the process.
And before you think you’re safe? People can get it too. Animals and infected mosquitoes transmit Rift Valley Fever. The symptoms are much like Corona and starts with fever, fatigue, body pains and dizziness. The last outbreak of Rift Valley fever was in 2010. 250 People contracted the virus and 25 lost their lives. 14 thousand animals were affected and 8000 died. Although more severe cases in humans can include eye disease, Hemorrhagic fever and inflammation of the brain, most people survive it, but most animals don’t.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Can South Africa's former world class immunology centre produce enough vaccines in time to prevent a countrywide epidemic or has the institution imploded on itself?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Why is a world class South African immunology centre not delivering much needed vaccines while scientists predict a country-wide epidemic?
metadata.Summary: The wellbeing of the South African livestock sector is hanging in the balance amidst the heavy rain season that may result in a countrywide epidemic that can only be prevented by vaccination. But, are the enough vaccines available and why is the state mum? The world class Onderstepoot Biological products vaccination plant was supposed to be upgraded in 2014 to enable it to research, produce and distribute much needed animal vaccinations. The highly specialised state owned veterinary science centre was given 500 million Rand to meet this need. It is the sole producer of vaccines that the agricultural sector cannot function without. And although the private sector produces the same vaccines, the state does not allow its distribution. Now it seems that no knows what happened to the money and whether the vaccine plant was upgraded at all.
metadata.Further information: Imagine there was only one institution in the world able to produce vaccines that prevent devastating epidemics in animals and people? Well, Onderstepoort was that institution; the pride and joy of South Africa’s veterinary science. Now, there is not much left of this world class research centre and the worst is, the vaccines will be desperately needed this year. In 2022, cadre deployment, misappropriation of state funds reminiscent of the state capture years under Jacob Zuma will become painfully visible in the Agricultural sector. Scientists, organised agriculture, the SA red meat association, retailers and farmers are holding their breaths as the anticipation of the outbreak of Rift valley fever is lurking on the horizon. Given the heavy rainy season, scientists and experts predict that the virus can hit South Africa hard. Mosquito larvas that have been dormant in dams and lakes across the country for over 10 years during the extended drought, can hatch as soon as February and spread countrywide in a matter of weeks. Rift Valley fever along with bluetongue disease and African horse sickness will cause mass devastation in the livestock sector if immediate solutions are not actioned and this will require decisive political will. Scientists and experts predict a massive shortage of vaccines for South Africa and the African continent at large. And that is all because of mismanagement of one of the country’s key scientific institutions. Treasury gave Onderstepoort Biological Products 500 million Rand in 2014 to develop a vaccine plant. This was never done. Instead 100 million was spent on the upgrading of offices and the payment of inflated salaries to people with no knowledge of vaccines or agriculture. This cannot be fixed overnight. Luckily, top former scientists who departed from Onderstepoort developed a world class laboratory in Pretoria where the vaccines are being developed. Designedbiologix is able to avail vaccines for Rift Valley fever, bluetongue disease and horse sickness in time before the breakout, but government is not coming to the party. The laboratory has been waiting four years for its license. And now, it may be too late, except if the department of agriculture fast tracks the process. And before you think you’re safe? People can get it too. Animals and infected mosquitoes transmit Rift Valley Fever. The symptoms are much like Corona and starts with fever, fatigue, body pains and dizziness. The last outbreak of Rift Valley fever was in 2010. 250 People contracted the virus and 25 lost their lives. 14 thousand animals were affected and 8000 died. Although more severe cases in humans can include eye disease, Hemorrhagic fever and inflammation of the brain, most people survive it, but most animals don’t.
